cards.text: Paul and Barnabas preached side by side on their first trip, and now they're back in Antioch, teaching. Some time later, Paul turns to Barnabas with that look on his face. The 'I've got an IDEA' look, which in my experience means somebody's about to pack a bag.

cards.question: Paul has an idea for Barnabas. Where does Paul want to go?

answers.text: Back to every town where they preached
Up to Jerusalem for another meeting
Down to Egypt to start somewhere new

cards.text: Barnabas wants to bring John, also called Mark. Paul thinks it's best NOT to, because Mark went with them once before, and let's just say Paul still remembers how that went.

cards.question: Why doesn't Paul want Mark on the trip?

answers.text: Mark wanted to stay in Antioch

cards.question: Barnabas wants Mark to come. Paul doesn't. True or false: Paul and Barnabas settle it and stay together.

cards.text: Their disagreement is so sharp that they part company, and Barnabas grabs Mark and gets on a boat. I spent years in a junk drawer listening to dead batteries argue over who had more charge left, so trust me, I know an argument nobody's backing down from.

cards.question: Barnabas takes Mark and sails for ___.
Barnabas is gone with Mark. Who does Paul choose as his new partner?

cards.text: Paul and Silas head out, and the brothers commend them to the grace of the Lord. Then Paul travels through Syria and Cilicia.

cards.question: As Paul travels through Syria and Cilicia, he goes along ___ the churches.

cards.text: Next stop, Derbe, then Lystra. And in Lystra, Paul finds a disciple named Timothy.

cards.question: Timothy is the son of a believing ___ woman and a ___ father.
True or false: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium speak well of Timothy.

cards.text: Paul wants Timothy on the team, so he takes him and circumcises him. After all that arguing in Jerusalem over circumcision, I KNOW your eyebrow just went up, because mine went up so high it knocked my hat off.

answers.text: The Jews there knew his father was Greek
The Jerusalem letter said he had to
Timothy asked Paul to do it first

cards.text: Then the team goes town to town, handing out the decisions from the apostles and elders in Jerusalem. They're delivering the mail now, and I promise you, this is NOT another expired coupon nobody asked for.

cards.question: As Paul's team delivers the Jerusalem decisions town to town, what happens to the churches?

answers.text: They grow in numbers every day
They argue over the new rules
They send the letter back unread

cards.text: Paul's team is on the move, ready to speak the word wherever they go. But in the province of Asia, somebody puts a stop to it.

cards.question: Who stops Paul's team from speaking the word in the province of Asia?

cards.text: So they travel through Phrygia and Galatia. Then at the border of Mysia, they try a new direction: Bithynia.

cards.question: True or false: The Spirit of Jesus lets Paul's team enter Bithynia.

cards.text: So they pass by Mysia and go down to Troas. Friend, this is me in a stranger's house looking for the bathroom: closet, NOPE, closet, NOPE, ANOTHER closet.
Then during the night in Troas, Paul has a vision. Not one of those dreams where you show up to work in your apron and nothing else matches. A real vision.

cards.question: In his vision, Paul sees a man of ___ standing there.
The man of Macedonia in Paul's vision is pleading with him. What is he asking Paul to do?

answers.text: Stay far away from their land
Pray for their king from afar

cards.question: Paul has just seen the man of Macedonia pleading for help. What does the team do?

answers.text: Get ready to leave right away
Send a letter to Macedonia first

cards.question: They conclude that God has called them to preach the ___ to the people of Macedonia.

cards.text: And look close, friend: the one telling this story stops saying 'they' and starts saying 'we.' Pack a bag, because this trip is just getting started.

findings.problem: The card says Paul and Barnabas preached together on their first trip and are now back in Antioch teaching. These facts come from outside the passage (Acts 13-14 and Acts 15:35) and have no reference. The card cites only Acts 15:36.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Silas shows up for the first time as the answer to this card, and card 9 doesn't say who he is either. The baker is never told who Silas is (Acts 15:22, 32). With no setup, the pick between Silas, Judas Barsabbas and Apollos is pure luck.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke relies on "all that arguing in Jerusalem over circumcision." That comes from Acts 15:1-29, which is outside the passage. It has no reference and is never set up in this lesson, so the eyebrow joke has nothing to land on.

rule.text: A callback only works if its setup came earlier in this lesson or conversation.

findings.problem: The Jerusalem dispute over circumcision is stated as a Bible fact with no reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "This is NOT another expired coupon nobody asked for" calls back the drawer's coupon without saying it was from the drawer. The comparison also doesn't match the action of delivering decisions, so it reads as "huh?"

rule.text: Bakers know he spent years in a junk drawer, from onboarding. The drawer's small details, like the batteries, the key or the coupon, only come up when the line says what they are, like "the dead batteries I shared that drawer with."

findings.problem: "Show up to work in your apron and nothing else matches" reads like the dream of showing up with nothing on but an apron. That is innuendo, and the line is muddled enough that a stranger would say "huh?"

rule.text: No cursing, crude humor, innuendo, or social or political commentary.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences: "Then during the night in Troas, Paul has a vision." / "Not one of those dreams..." / "A real vision."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says the man is pleading with Paul, so "Stay far away from their land" doesn't fit at all. That makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
